prompt: State what is meant by a systematic error, and give one example of a systematic error that could arise when measuring the fall time of an object using a manually operated stopwatch.
hints: Explain how systematic errors affect measured values relative to the true value.
Consider human physiological limitations when timing an event manually.
solution: A systematic error causes readings to differ from the true value by a consistent amount (or in the same direction) each time the measurement is repeated [1 mark]. Example: The reaction time delay of the experimenter in starting or stopping the stopwatch [1 mark].
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Define systematic error: readings consistently higher or lower than the true value by a fixed amount or fraction [1 mark].
Step 2: State an appropriate timing example: experimenter reaction time delay in pressing the start/stop button [1 mark].

provenance.independence_statement: Authored independently to test experimental error awareness in kinematics.
